title: Application UI admin workspace

story.need: manage content through a coherent, responsive administration workspace built from governed Application UI patterns
story.outcome: content, media, settings, publishing, and revision work remain clear and efficient in light or dark mode

scope: Replace the existing admin shell with a responsive stacked navigation shell
Provide explicit light, dark, and system appearance choices with a persistent user preference
Rebuild content lists, page creation, media, and settings with shared Application UI controls and feedback
Use a three-pane desktop editor with block outline, primary form, and contextual publishing inspector
Convert secondary editor panes to accessible drawers on narrower screens
Preserve all existing draft, preview, publish, revision, media, and settings behavior
nonGoals: Changing the public-site theme or Marketing block renderer
Changing content schemas, permissions, revision semantics, or MCP contracts
Copying licensed source examples into documentation
Adding new administrative product capabilities unrelated to the redesign
dataRequirements: The appearance preference is one of system, light, or dark and is stored locally per browser
Navigation state derives from the current route and is not persisted as content
Editor pane selection is ephemeral interface state and never enters a content revision
Existing page, media, settings, revision, and audit data remain unchanged
permissions: Only authenticated users on the existing allowlist may render the admin workspace
Presentation changes do not weaken existing service-layer authorization
Anonymous visitors cannot read administrative data or preferences from the server

acceptanceCriteria.given: an authenticated user on any admin route
acceptanceCriteria.when: the workspace renders on desktop or mobile
then: stacked navigation exposes Content, Media, Site settings, Reference catalog, View site, appearance, and account actions
the current destination and keyboard focus are visually unambiguous
mobile navigation is operable as an accessible disclosure

acceptanceCriteria.given: a user editing a page on a wide viewport
then: the block outline, primary editing form, and publishing inspector remain independently scannable
save, preview, and publish state stays visible
the same secondary panes open as accessible drawers on narrower viewports

acceptanceCriteria.given: a user chooses system, light, or dark appearance
acceptanceCriteria.when: they navigate or reload the admin
then: the preference persists in that browser
system mode follows the operating-system preference
all admin controls, dialogs, tables, states, and focus indicators meet WCAG AA contrast

acceptanceCriteria.given: existing pages, media, settings, and revisions
then: all existing authoring and publishing workflows remain available
mutations still call the shared application services
MCP behavior and public rendering remain unchanged

fixtures: page containing all seventeen block families
media library with portrait, landscape, and decorative images
site settings containing navigation, footer groups, theme, and redirects
light, dark, and system appearance preferences
verification: Admin shell route and appearance preference component tests
Desktop and mobile browser tests for every admin route
Keyboard navigation and focus-order tests for navigation, menus, drawers, and dialogs
Existing MCP contract, domain, build, UAT, and production verification loops
